names.goal-sip: Goal SIP: how much to invest
names.income-tax: Income tax: old vs new regime

labels.extraInterestForLongerTenure: Extra interest for the longer tenure

explain.sip: Each monthly instalment compounds at the expected return for the months it stays invested. The formula is FV = P × [((1 + i)^n − 1) ÷ i] × (1 + i), where i is the monthly rate and n the number of months.
explain.lumpsum: The amount grows at the expected return, compounded yearly: FV = P × (1 + r)^n.
explain.emi: EMI = P × i × (1 + i)^n ÷ [(1 + i)^n − 1], where P is the loan, i the monthly rate and n the number of months. Early EMIs are mostly interest; the share of principal rises over time.
explain.fd: Banks compound term deposits quarterly: maturity = P × (1 + r ÷ 4)^(4 × years).
explain.goal: Today's cost is inflated to the target date, existing savings and SIPs are grown at the expected return, and the monthly SIP closes the remaining gap.
explain.retirementCorpus: Expenses are inflated to retirement, then the corpus is the present value of an inflation-indexed annuity from retirement to life expectancy at the post-retirement return.
explain.incomeTax: Both regimes are computed on the same income: standard deduction, slab tax, section 87A rebate, surcharge and 4% cess. Deductions under 80C, 80D, 80CCD(1B) and 24(b) apply only in the old regime.
explain.termCover: Needs-based: the present value of replacing income (growing with inflation) until retirement, plus loans and goals, minus liquid assets and existing cover.
explain.default: Standard time-value-of-money formulas with the inputs and assumptions shown. Every result records the rule-pack version used.

cashflow.title: Cash flow and budgeting
cashflow.why: A savings rate of 20% or more is what funds every other goal.

emergency.title: Emergency fund
emergency.why: Six months of essentials keeps a bad month from forcing bad decisions.

debt.title: Debt
debt.why: EMIs under 35% of income and no revolving card debt leave room to invest.

insurance.title: Insurance protection
insurance.why: Term cover of 10 to 15× income and adequate health cover protect the plan itself.

investments.title: Investments and allocation
investments.why: An age-appropriate equity share and no idle cash make money work.

retirement.title: Retirement readiness
retirement.why: Projected corpus against what retirement will actually cost.

goals.title: Goal readiness
goals.why: Share of goal value funded on the current trajectory.

hygiene.title: Tax and hygiene
hygiene.why: Nominations and a will make sure the money reaches the right people.

items.fixOverspend: Bring expenses under income: you are spending about ₹{gap} a month more than you earn.
items.clearHighCostDebt: Clear high-cost debt first: {share}% of your debt is credit-card or personal-loan debt above 15%.
items.raiseTermCover: Raise term life cover to about ₹{target} ({multiple}× annual income). Compare three insurers on claim-settlement ratio and premium.
items.raiseHealthCover: Raise health cover: you have {ratio}% of the recommended amount for your city.
items.setNominations: Set nominations on every bank account, policy and investment.
items.buildEmergencyFund: Build the emergency fund from {months} to {target} months of essential expenses in a liquid fund or sweep-in FD.
items.reduceEmiLoad: EMIs take {share}% of income. Prepay the costliest loan or extend tenure to get under 35%.
items.raiseSavingsRate: Raise the savings rate from {rate}% to {target}%: automate the difference on salary day.
items.rebalance: Rebalance: equity is {equity}% of financial assets against a target of about {target}%.
items.deployIdleCash: Move idle cash ({share}% of financial assets beyond the emergency fund) into a plan.
items.fundGoals: Goals are {ready}% funded on the current path; raise SIPs or push out the flexible ones.
items.retirementSip: Retirement is {ready}% on track against a corpus of about ₹{corpus}; start or raise the retirement SIP.
items.writeWill: Write a simple will; with dependants or after 40 it is the cheapest protection there is.
items.annualReview: Re-run the check-up once a year and after any life event.

legal.disclaimerBody: My Money & Me provides educational content and tools only. Nothing on this site is investment, insurance, tax or legal advice, and nothing is a recommendation to buy or sell any product. We never name a specific fund, bank or insurer. Calculators and the check-up use the assumptions shown and the India rule pack version displayed on each result; outcomes are not guaranteed. Consult a SEBI-registered investment adviser or a qualified professional before acting.
legal.privacyBody: We collect no personal data on the public site beyond anonymised, aggregated analytics. Calculator inputs and quick-check answers stay in your browser. When accounts launch, financial data will be encrypted, exportable and deletable by you at any time, held in an Indian data region, and never sold or used for advertising. Children under 18 cannot hold accounts; parents manage child profiles that hold no contact data.
legal.termsBody: The site is free to use. Content is original and may be shared with attribution and a link. You agree not to misrepresent the site's tools as advice, scrape content at scale, or attempt to disrupt the service.
legal.grievanceBody: For grievances under the Information Technology Act and the DPDP Act, write to grievance@mymoneyandme.in. We acknowledge within 48 hours and resolve within the statutory period.
legal.accessibilityBody: We aim for WCAG 2.2 AA across every language, with keyboard-operable calculators, 16 px minimum body text, high-contrast and dyslexia-friendly modes planned. Report an accessibility problem to hello@mymoneyandme.in.
